sources.reason: Repository-wide collection of IPL ROM, Human68k utilities and sound-driver listings. Sampled ATTRIB has numeric labels and hardware/OS includes; semantic depth varies, and no global completeness or matching claim was independently verified.

Whole-repository collection includes substantive iffparse C reconstruction and per-library knowledge. Upstream says roughly 1,230 library builds are verbatim hunk-word images, not recovered semantic source. Do not interpret the 1,482-library documentation claim as 1,482 fully understood implementations.

Executable-derived BBS-PC! reconstruction with login, modem, menu, message and file modules. Earlier Amiga-focused deferral is resolved for DOS scope only; README targets Microsoft C 4.0 under DOS, not an Amiga port. Duplicate-case filenames and no independent build remain caveats.

Nested hd/utils contains readable BASIC listings paired with PRGs for drive setup, formatting, partition queries and clock control. Sampled ADD DRIVE identifies CMD HD and SCSI addressing. Resolves prior root-only deferral; this is utility-source recovery, not a reconstructed drive firmware.

Magic Desk music-visualizer/game cartridge research with bank extraction, control mapping and reproducible VICE probes. Generated assembly and cartridge bytes are deliberately not committed; this is analysis tooling, not a complete restored game source.

Interrupt-driven three-event game, VRAM helpers and inline dispatch tables documented in address-anchored annotations. Upstream reports byte-exact 16 KB reconstruction with a user-supplied ROM; no independent build or completeness verification performed.

Address-anchored analysis distinguishes event table order from text order and documents interrupt, state and drawing systems. Upstream reports byte-exact 16 KB reconstruction with a user-supplied ROM; no independent build or completeness verification performed.

Semantic annotations cover the interrupt-driven state machine, controllers, dispatch tables and graphics scripts. Upstream reports byte-exact 16 KB reconstruction with a user-supplied ROM; no independent build or completeness verification performed.

Annotations cover delayed anti-copy ROM writes, menu streams and VDP layout; sampled annotation contains malformed-looking text, so build correctness is not assumed. Upstream reports byte-exact 16 KB reconstruction with a user-supplied ROM; no independent build or completeness verification performed.

Semantic annotations identify interrupt scheduling, inline dispatch and two graphics interpreters. Upstream reports byte-exact 16 KB reconstruction with a user-supplied ROM; no independent build or completeness verification performed.
Native homebrew source with game logic, graphics and music resources. README requires its compatible SDCC version and batch build scripts; bundled compiler binaries were not executed.
Z80 main program and separate music/sprite source for ColecoVision. Sparse README is supplemented by source inspection; no runtime or build validation.
Assembly for declaration ROM, primary initialization, video driver and Easter egg. Author describes it as a codebase for explaining declaration ROMs, not a complete system ROM reconstruction.

MCP/REST research server, front end, trap database and 68k source-correlation workspace. Raw ROMs, full disassemblies and source overlays remain local/ignored; this is substantive tooling, not published complete ROM source.

Charles MacDonald demo reconstruction with video-register definitions and Jo Engine build. Author reports emulator/hardware behaviour and cable-specific limitations; those claims were not independently tested.

Distinct SDL3 backend port of the already tracked DOS C reconstruction. Sample entry point documents built-in mission/model fallback when GAME.DAT is absent. Port and verification claims are upstream claims; do not imply independently proven full-game coverage.

Logical C reconstruction and Ghidra annotations for the Katana sound driver, pinned to Soul Calibur's reference build. Source exposes MIDI-ring behaviour and uncertainty notes. Explicitly non-byte-matching; ARM audio CPU must not be misclassified as the console's SH-4 host.

Browser recreation using decoded original world/model/animation data and a Go multiplayer server. Story progression and broader original behaviour remain incomplete. Arcade cabinets use EmulatorJS, but core world recreation is separate native application logic, not a game-specific emulator wrapper.

Substantive JavaScript decoder/decompiler with state/context tracking, data walkers and Spectrum tape research. It is an experimental analysis tool; no IDA-equivalence or complete decompilation claim inferred.

Preservation archive of Segher's CIC analysis and SuperCIC key/lock implementations. Source identifies PIC16F630/676 targets and upstream authors. This is an attributed archive, not newly authored research or a 65C816 program.
ASM6f source targeting Japan/USA Rev A, with named RAM/constants, game data and PRG modules. Sampled constants describe pill, virus and multiplayer mechanics; build not independently run.
USA-version source using the author's SNES ROM Framework. Includes named game RAM, routines and asset extraction; requires a user-supplied clean ROM. No independent rebuild.

Traced and rewritten flash-cart menu using bass v14. Source notes incomplete commenting, and README says relocation would be needed for original byte layout; functional-equivalence claims do not establish byte matching.

Reconstructed CP/M loader and BIOS with commented machine-specific utilities. README explicitly limits operating-system disassembly to loader/BIOS, not the entire CCP/BDOS. Build and consistency targets exist but were not executed.

README describes bulk dis1600 output with inferred labels and some disabled analysis. Do not equate 178 raw listings with semantically recovered projects; review meaningful annotations before promotion.
Inspected Z80Decoder.cs has only an empty constructor. Project description overstates implemented decoder evidence; do not promote as a working decompiler.

README explicitly says not to use this source and points to gauze/Spudster-s-Revenge as final version. Current-upstream review remains open.

notes: Parent-only pass across 32 platform/type search lanes. Early searches produced fork clusters and unrelated fuzzy matches; metadata and canonical parent screening removed them. Full catalogue/source/decision screening avoided treating deferral as permanent exclusion. A .txt extension concealed readable BASIC source. One oversized Amiga recursive tree failed; bounded per-library traversal recovered evidence. Semantic source, automatic disassembly and verbatim hunk preservation are explicitly distinguished. Agent configuration alone leaves AI unknown. New ingestion suggestions: parent/redirect-aware screening before deep reads, preserve scope reasons on deferrals, and use bounded tree traversal with legacy source extensions. No new pipeline code changed in this pass. Validation exposed an ingestion limitation: decision URLs are append-only and unique, so two prior deferrals cannot receive a new promoted decision through the current API. Their projects, sources, audits and research event record the new outcome; historical deferrals remain unchanged. A future explicit supersession mechanism would preserve history while displaying the current outcome.
